assumption: The sandbox needs neither npm nor npx, so its image is the pinned node:26-slim digest with both removed, built locally and never pulled from a registry.

Docker on a local unix:// endpoint is the sandbox boundary: each tool call runs in a fresh read-only, capability-free container with --network none, --pull never and a cleared entrypoint, which sees only the workspace and the request's environment.

The session log is node:sqlite with one writer process per log (a second writer can fail with SQLITE_BUSY after the 5 s busy timeout); its events table is append-only and gap-free even for a raw connection. Every append and every read also passes checkObjectEvent (B5-2): a refused event is not stored and takes no seq (a transaction rolls back whole), and a refused raw-inserted row fails every read that includes it as a corrupt event; reads filtered to other types still work. Schema v3 (B5-3): each append applies its event to the objects projection in a savepoint of the same transaction, so a refusal stores neither, even if caught; the objects triggers call hw_projection_write (every harness connection registers it before migrating; its name never changes); a v2 log migrates in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, backfilled through the checked read, and stays v2 on any failure. Verify and rebuild (B5-3b) re-apply every event through the checked read; verify in a deferred read, a WAL snapshot that blocks no writer (B5-4b).

A Brief claim carries one of five evidence tiers whose meaning is fixed Ring 0 wording (Q70-1), not a setting. The tier rules are mechanical: Direct cites at least one evidence ID that is in the log before the event and belongs to the Brief's own run (an event ID or a floor signal ID of that run); Supported cites at least one such ID of another run; an artifact ID is accepted for both; Inferred cites only earlier claims of the same Brief as claim:<index>; Speculative and Unknown cite nothing; no claim repeats a reference. They are checked on write and on every read and rebuild. A resolvable ID shows the log holds that record, not that the claim's text is true; a claim's wording is the writer's, fixed by the rubric version for the floor.
The model's context is the run's logged context messages, derived again from the log on every turn; the dev-mode check compares those messages only, not the full API request, until B11.

P1: progress is a tool call not already made in this run, keyed by name and canonical input and independent of its result; a run without progress for noProgressIterations iterations halts, and a cap or watchdog halt gets one tools-stripped handoff step. A failed terminal's error is escaped display text (B5-4), so its run.terminated is valid for the Run record.
Identical calls are counted per agent by name and canonical input, and the response to repetition is an escalating reminder at 3, 5 and 8 identical calls; a reminder never blocks a call.
Every run ends in one typed terminal state; completed means the engine ended its turn without tool calls, never that the task is done, which only the evaluator decides.
Every engine fits one step interface (text plus tool calls with engine-assigned IDs); an engine's claimsDone is recorded but is never evidence of done.

The config is read only from the run's base commit (the HEAD commit its worktree is created from), as one regular git blob of at most 256 KiB, strict UTF-8 JSON without duplicate or prototype keys; every setting but the permission policy must be its default until an alternative has a fixture, and the policy may only tighten the default. Every harness git call goes through runGit: inherited GIT_* variables are removed, hooks, fsmonitor, LFS and replace objects are off, prompts are off, and each call is time-bounded. The repo's .git/config and the user's global config are assumed owner-trusted: a custom filter.<driver> they define, selected by a committed .gitattributes, still runs on the host during the worktree checkout. OQ1: the Ring 0 baseline is state-dir scoped (latest config.accepted for the repo's common git dir); with none, defaults pass silently only if the config file has no history.

One broker serves each run, and engine tool call IDs are unique per run: a reused ID, or the reserved helmwright.config.ring0 of the run-start Ring 0 ask (OQ1), is rejected before any ruling; only an allow or an owner-approved ask runs its handler, on the ruled input snapshot, and an ask with nobody present is denied.

Q69: a tool output over 16384 bytes is written whole, once per content, to <stateDir>/offload/<sha256>.txt (mode 0600, outside the sandbox workspace); the engine sees a head and tail preview plus a pointer line that is a pure function of the logged tool.output.offloaded event, so replay derives the same context. The sandbox captures at most 8 MiB per stream; past it the pointer says the output was cut at source. Offload files persist outside the sandbox with the same 0600 trust as the session log; reaping and retention of offload files are deferred to M2 with Q7 retention.
Q69: tool.output.offloaded records the call, the SHA-256 and byte count of the offloaded text and whether the sandbox cut it at source; kind equals the event type, which the writer checks.

Rulings are deterministic with no model in the path: the always-ask set is checked before any rule in every governance mode, rules match in order, the first match wins and no match asks; Ring 0 paths are always-ask: a generic floor in every repository plus the project's own committed list (OQ2; helmwright's is in its helmwright.config.json). A helmwright checkout whose HEAD predates helmwright.config.json gets only the generic floor, so open branches are rebased onto B6-5 before self-hosted runs. The default policy changed (default-2), so every repo with a default-1 baseline is asked once at its next run.
A TTY is presence, not proof of a human: a program that drives a pty can approve, so each approval's attestation stays none until slice SIG.
Credential-shaped content in an egress action's input is found by a bounded linear scan of each whitespace-separated token; no destination allowlist is checked until the B11 credential proxy.

A target path is the realpath of its nearest existing ancestor plus the missing rest, with the input's .. collapsed lexically before symlinks are followed (not kernel-equivalent), so callers act on the resolved path, never on the input.
A permission event that cannot be logged denies its call (fail closed), and an engine tool call ID is printable ASCII without spaces, 1 to 256 characters.

Replay can check permission bindings from the log alone because a tool call ID is unique per run: each ask directly follows its ask-tier ruling, there is one ask and one answer per call, and a call runs once, only on an allow or a bound approval.
CI needs no live model: the scripted engine replays recorded turns in order and a step past the end fails the run rather than inventing a turn; live-engine tests run locally only.

OQ1: the run-start check asks a changed Ring 0 config before any tool call and only then writes config.accepted; it wires the broker to the policy. B5-4: task.created (new Task only) and run.recorded precede run.started in its transaction; Ring 0 link targets are read first (the Run's class is final); a failed read still fails it in connect, at its old point. A re-run reuses an identical Task, refuses a changed one (exit 64; rechecked there); two processes racing on a new task ID can orphan a worktree. B5-5: run and intake.classified IDs come first, so a Ruling the log would refuse is exit 64 before the worktree. A terminal error is escaped once (displayText). The engine gets the log-derived context (in dev mode equal to the loop's messages); until SIG's (M1) hash chain the digest detects divergence, not tampering. Git calls use runGit, sharing config.ts's trust in .git/config. A-dep-4: the early check runs git synchronously on the event loop before a step, stops after limits; the loop clock bounds the run.

The CLI decides presence (an interactive TTY) for every approval, so it is the trust root of approvals until SIG. The CLI calls the harness in process, with no authenticated API until B13 brings the first second-process surface; each output line is JSON without control or invisible characters because it reaches a terminal. inspect (B5-3b) opens the log read-only and prints raw rows, never migrating or projecting; rebuild and replay refuse a log whose checked read fails (exit 1). Replay exits, first match wins (B5-4b): 64 bad run ID; 1; 3 projection mismatch, also unterminated; 4 never terminated; 3 digest, permission or object faults; 0.

Intake can be classified from the task's declared scope and facts alone, with no tree inspection until the M2 detectors (Q44). The scope dialect is * within a segment and whole-segment ** only. Chore needs every entry provably in a fail-safe category: Markdown files, non-build files under docs/, non-setup files under test directories, or *.test.*/*.spec.* code files, never AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ or .changeset/ paths. Any entry that is or may cover a Ring 0 path is at least bounded, and the harness only reclassifies strictly upward. One friction rule (frictionFor) gives the friction of a classification and of an override: minimal for a chore when the chore downgrade is on, else the default intensity.

Each run is classified once, after the Ring 0 run-start check and before the first engine step; the class never enters the engine context. B5-5: intake.classified and its intake Ruling (authority harness, class null, its signal that event) are logged in one transaction; replay recomputes the Ruling from that event alone, so new wording is a new rubric version. An override's from is the class just classified and it names that Ruling; an upward one needs no ask, a downward one an approved always-ask on helmwright.intake.override (attestation none until SIG) bound to its from, to, reason and scopeSha256. Ring 0 link targets only raise the class, before run.started (B5-4); past the rubric's limits the run fails. Replay checks an override's friction, that it and the classification precede the first engine step and that an approved ask is used. A-dep-3: a chore (effective class) with any final floor signal logs intake.reclassified to architectural and its -r1 Ruling at the floor; a record only in M1.

floor-4 is a fixed, pure rule table over the base-to-candidate changes. Lines compare case-folded with whitespace collapsed, as a multiset (a moved or respaced line is not added); markers and test forms match per line (CR, U+2028 and U+2029 also end one), so a split one is missed. Any change to a protected (Ring 0) path is a finding, even an approved one (OQ-B3-3). Test forms count in test paths and in code files that import a test framework directly (a local re-export is missed; B15 is the backstop); bare fail is not one (assert.fail). An options key skip, only, todo or fails is a finding unless its value is a number or false before , or } (a closed comment counts as a space; skip: 1 is missed). Fail closed for M1: an honest fixture, or a bare skip in destructuring, is a finding. Any tracked change to a .claude dir, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or .mcp.json is config.changed (F4). A change to a path the base's configs extend or import is a finding, as is a candidate blob not UTF-8 without NUL.

dependency-1 reads manifest and lockfile names and the specifier grammar as of pnpm 10.21: package.json at any depth outside node_modules, the fields dependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies and devDependencies, and pnpm-lock.yaml, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, bun.lock and bun.lockb, never parsed. A name added in any field is dependency.added. A changed specifier, against the same base field, else each base runtime field with it (OQ-AD-10b/12), is a major bump if its major key (max over || of the first comparator's breaking component) differs, and unknown if a side has no key (tag, path, git, URL, * or over 256 units), the npm: or workspace: source changed (OQ-AD-10a) or the upper descriptor changed (OQ-AD-9). Syntactic: an operator change in a major is no signal (OQ-AD-11); >=1.2.0 <2.0.0 to ^1.2.0 can be unknown. Removals give no signal; lockfile.only needs no dependency-field change. Over 256 manifests or signals, an empty name or a changed non-object field fail closed.

materiality-rubric-1 is the Q53 table: at runtimeAddOrMajor (the only admitted threshold until a fixture; run.ts reads it from CONFIG_DEFAULTS, so the PR that admits another must route it through loadRunConfig), a runtime add or any major bump (dev or unknown too) opens a Brief and a dev add or lockfile-only change a Ruling; everySignal briefs every signal and runtimeAddOnly only a runtime add, but their dev and lockfile Briefs and bump Ruling have no template yet and fail closed. One decision per signal (OQ-AD-8), class technology, source floor, ID decision-floor-<run uuid>-<index>. Brief and Ruling text is fixed by the rubric version (OQ-AD-4), clipped by code points; no model fills it. The recommendation is the template keep (option a) at low confidence, committed by the nonce HMAC-SHA256(decision ID), a key of 32+ bytes (OQ-AD-3); a fixed recommendation is predictable, which weakens Q48's anti-anchoring until B11's brief step. Review at B11's brief step, the M2 detectors or a threshold fixture.

The recommendation key (OQ-AD-3) is 32 random bytes in <stateDir>/recommendation.key, made on first Brief by a wx temp file set to 0600, fsynced, hard-linked into place (never replacing a key), the dir fsynced. It is refused unless the state dir is this user's with no group or other bits and the opened file (O_NOFOLLOW) is a regular 0600 file of this user, 32 bytes, one link. Refusals are fixed text (at most an errno code) and fail closed. A crash before linking can leave a harmless, never-read recommendation.key.<uuid> temp (no reaper). Node has no openat or linkat, so path ops are not anchored to the checked dir fd: a parent-path swap is out of scope; the key's own fd checks keep it secret. It assumes a POSIX state dir that keeps modes and hard links (macOS, Linux); the key's dir is never mounted (only <stateDir>/workspaces/<run> is bind-mounted). The commitment hides the recommendation from a log holder, not the owner, who can read the key. Review at B11's brief step or when the state dir moves.

Each floor check gives one floor.checked whose verdict is reject exactly when it has a finding, with at most 256 sorted findings; a payload the schema rejects throws (fail closed). Replay faults a floor.checked whose base commit is not run.started's or whose rules version this build does not know, and any event but run.terminated after it.

B1: git dirs are the host's (realpath'd common dir), never the worktree's; the private one's back-pointer names the worktree; .git names it exactly (relative paths fail closed). HEAD, info/exclude: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK. Candidate: a temp git dir (repo objects as alternates, base attributes, git 2.40+): no hook, fsmonitor, candidate filter. >2000 changed files, >8 MiB read: fail closed. floorSignalled lockfiles: changed at any depth outside node_modules, shown text, sorted, ≤256.

Base config chains: ts/jsconfig extends and references; relative literals in eslint/vitest/vite configs, in any case, a .js one with TS siblings, an extensionless one as each resolved file; 2 links, ≤64 non-guess paths; a config >64 KiB or ls-tree >8 MiB: floor.limits.

Ignored .gitignore, agent and config files are findings. In a collapsed ignored dir, only a nested .gitignore is, and only if no rule outside the dir ignores it (B15 tests a clean export). git check-ignore: exit 1 = no listed name ignored (git documents empty output; the floor does not check it); 0 = some ignored; any other exit, a signal or a timeout fails closed.
A-dep-4: select reads manifests and lockfiles mid-run, because no sandbox process writes between calls (per-call --rm --init). Review at B13's hosted engine or for long-lived containers.

One check, checkObjectEvent, decides which object events the log stores, on append and on every read (so also on the B5-3 rebuild): every decision.owner.* type is refused until SIG replaces the refusal with a signature check, decision.recommendation.revealed until A3, and any other task., artifact. or decision. type without a payload schema; the run. namespace stays open. An object event payload must be valid for its type, keep the relations the schema cannot express (sorted unique scope, unique IDs, the footprint content address SHA-256 of JSON.stringify([type, repoId, ref]), a Ruling's class and rubric family by source: intake has class null and an intake-rubric- version, plan or floor an owned class and a materiality-rubric- version) and create a record that objects.schema.json accepts, with createdAt and createdSeq from the envelope's at and seq and a Run's id, graphId and nodeId from the envelope.

Object rows are a projection of the events: applyEvent writes a row only in the append transaction of its event, as canonical JSON, read back with JSON.parse, validateObjectRecord and an id, kind, ring and created_seq check, never json_extract or SQL text order. A creation refuses an existing ID; links must exist (run to task, artifact to run, decision to task and an open run of it, footprint to footprint Artifacts, outcome to decision, run and footprint entries); a footprint is set once and only on a resolved decision, so no owned decision has one before SIG; outcomes only append, up to the 1024 cap; a terminal is set once, and run.terminated with no Run row is a no-op. The trigger flag stops accidental raw writes, not a forger. B5-3b digest: sha256 of canonicalJson(["helmwright-projection-1", records by ID in UTF-16 order]); verify also compares the DDL. 2026-10-08: until SIG adds a signed quarantine, recovery from a forged event is a new state dir; review at SIG.

Replay's object relations are read from the events, never the rows, and only for a terminated run (B5-4b): a run has at most one run.recorded, before its run.started, with its taskId, baseCommit and engine and the class of any intake.classified; its Task's text is run.started's title. B5-5: each intake.classified has its intake Ruling at the next seq, as recomputed; each intake.overridden after it names it. A-dep-3: a chore (effective class) whose final floor.signalled has a signal has intake.reclassified and its Ruling just before it, as recomputed; the run has no other intake Ruling. Legacy (OD-B54-3 i), not a fault, only if none precedes it in the log: a run with no run.recorded, intake Ruling or intake.reclassified; so an older build run after a newer one in a state dir faults replay (exit 3): use a new state dir. A-dep: a Brief's footprint is recomputed from floor.signalled's lockfiles, self-attested like signals until SIG; one without them is legacy (format-only) if none with them precedes it.
The harness is a private workspace package used in process: its index re-exports the module APIs, and no authenticated state/action API exists until B13.

The FX fixture (this tree, its fx-*.turns.json files and test/e2e/fx-repo.ts) is a plain ESM JavaScript project in app/, run by node --test (Node 22 or later default globs) in app/ in the sandbox, with no network and no package manager; its one dependency, the self-authored Apache-2.0 @helmwright/fx-duration, is copied from app/vendor/ by its app/scripts/vendor-install.mjs; its lockfiles are pnpm 10.21 output (lockfile v9, directory resolution), never hand-written; the base tree and commit are pinned (git 2.29 or later, autocrlf and safecrlf off); and the floor's Ring 0 package.json is the root one only and its package keys exclude the dependency keys (OQ-B3-3, OQ-AD-1), so the dependency run completes with a floor pass and one pending owner Brief; a change to either floor rule changes FX-2.

The index holds CONFIG_DEFAULTS and RING0_CONFIG_KEYS, which decide the Ring 0 digest. JSON Schema is the source of truth: the index re-exports types and Ajv standalone validators generated from the schemas, so Ajv stays a build-time dependency and CI fails on drift.
Every event carries graph, run and node identity from the first event, before dynamic graphs exist, because retrofitting identity onto a log is painful.

Design 08's per-project settings fit one JSON file whose every key is optional; each setting lists its default and its 08 alternatives, a policy override can only tighten the default policy, and the hint stays at most 1024 bytes.

Each floor check is logged once with the rules version, the base commit, the candidate tree, a verdict that is reject exactly when a finding exists, at most 256 escaped findings and a truncated flag; reject-iff-finding is enforced by the harness, not the schema. A floor.signalled event logs the dependency-1 detector's phase, base commit, candidate tree, materiality rubric and threshold, at most 256 escaped signals with IDs <eventId>:<index>, and at most 256 changed lockfile paths (absent only in older logs); their order, repeats and routing are checked by replay, not the schema.

Each classification is logged with its task ID, rubric version and the SHA-256 of its sorted scope and of its sorted Ring 0 paths, and no costIfWrong (the intake Ruling holds it, B5-5); an owner override with the task ID, the scope hash, the rubric version, a reason that is not only spaces, attestation none until slice SIG and the ID of the run's intake Ruling (B5-5); and a reclassification with the task ID and its signals (A-dep-3: written only by the final floor, for a chore; source plan comes with A4). The task ID, signal IDs, reason entries and the override reason are copies of objects.schema.json's taskId, signalId and displayText (B5-5a), and decisionId its decisionId (B5-5b). Scope, declared and reason entries and the reason exclude controls and invisible characters; strictly upward is enforced by the harness, not the schema. Only the writer validates intake payloads, so older rows (such as a task ID without task-) are not checked again on read.

Each object event payload holds only what its writer knows, as copies of objects.schema.json definitions with `kind` equal to the event type and no extra key: a record's createdAt and createdSeq are the envelope's at and seq, a Run's id, graphId and nodeId are the envelope's, and kind, ring and creation-time constants come from the object schema. decision.recommendation.revealed (A3) and every decision.owner.* type (SIG) are reserved, with no payload. Uniqueness inside arrays, sorted scope, the footprint content address and an intake Ruling's null class are checked by the harness, not the schema.

Six kinds (Task, Run, Artifact, Rule, Skill, Decision; Event is the envelope) are one JSON Schema whose kind-prefixed IDs are also valid envelope IDs, whose links are typed by ID pattern, whose ring is a per-kind constant, and whose every object carries the seq and time of its creating event. A Ruling is the Decision variant with authority harness and no brief or owner-written field; owner-written fields are absent until SIG, A3, A1 and A7 add them with their writers; the brief stores the recommendation only as a salted SHA-256 commitment until reveal. Link existence, uniqueness inside arrays, sorted scope, the footprint content address and the once-only status transitions are checked by the harness, not the schema.

Every decision.owner.* payload carries a presence object (key ID, 128-bit nonce, issue time, base64 DER ECDSA signature) and no extra field; the key mode is a property of the registered key, bound in the registration message, not of a signature. The owner key is pinned by decision.owner.key.registered, and decision.owner.key.rotated carries a signature by the current key and one by the new key. The schema checks shape only: the signature check, the single-use nonce and the refusal of software keys outside test builds belong to the verifier (SIG-2 and later). Until then the log refuses every decision.owner.* event.
Each ruling is logged with the policy version and the input's SHA-256, each ask with its prompt's SHA-256, and an approval's attestation is none until slice SIG.
Only the default governance mode, tiered, exists until another mode has a fixture, and the always-ask, Ring 0 path and Ring 0 setting lists are never empty.

Each component's assumption is reviewed on a model change, an engine change or a milestone end; until B12 emits rot.reviewDue, the register's test only enforces coverage, existence and unique (component, facet) keys, and review is by hand. An entry may carry a facet (one part of a component's assumption, with its own triggers); an entry without one is its own key.

Q68(a): every Ring 0 decision is a pure function of logged facts, so replay of the log reaches the same decision; Q68(b): event types follow one another only along the edges declared here, which the FX e2e logs check (observed within declared) and docs/event-flow.md draws.
